/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Language.RuleEval
  Evaluating a rule over a trace, and checking it before any trace.

  `verdicts` combines the binder classes, the applicability and the obligation per instant
  (Kleene, `verdictAt`). `check` finds from the syntax every defect the evaluator would otherwise
  report as `malformed` or `unboundVariable`; its doc comment lists them. `checkReading`
  names the parameters and aggregates the reading lacks, over the rule and the rules it composes,
  with their concept calls expanded; `Concept.checkReading` the aggregates a concept's body names.

  `Concept.check` holds a concept to the same standard on every admissible instantiation of
  its formals, with its calls expanded. `Concept.callDefects` holds every concept call to the
  callee's signature before expansion loses it.

  Nothing under Rules/ or Concepts/ imports this file; Grounding, Manifest and Monitor do.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Concept
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Semantics
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.EvalFast

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Rule
open Semantics

/-- A rule's formula as evaluated: every comparison over a `cond` decided by cases, through the
    sub-expression cache (`evalFastAll`, whose every stored value is the one `evalAll` gives). -/
def evalRuleFormula (c : SemCtx) (φ : Formula) : Array R := evalFastAll c (Formula.elimCond φ)

/-- Every binder's class holds for its bound track and the applicability holds, per instant. -/
def engagedAll (r : Rule) (c : SemCtx) : Array R :=
  Temporal.allOf c.n (r.binders.map (fun b => evalRuleFormula c b.cls) ++ [evalRuleFormula c r.applicability])

/-- The verdict at every instant. -/
def verdicts (r : Rule) (c : SemCtx) : Array Verdict :=
  Array.zipWith verdictAt (r.engagedAll c) (evalRuleFormula c r.obligation)

/-- The rule as a three-valued statement per instant: complied with (true), violated (false), or
    unknown. Not engaged counts as complied with — a rule that does not apply is not broken. -/
def asRAll (r : Rule) (c : SemCtx) : Array R :=
  (r.verdicts c).map fun v => match v with
    | .compliant | .notApplicable => R.t
    | .violated => R.f
    | .unknown w => ⟨.u, w⟩

/-- Structural well-formedness apart from having a binder: binders named and distinct, the id
    set, every assumption and intention used declared, every intention id well-formed, every
    operationalization bounding its standard by atoms, primitives or concepts. -/
def wellFormedBody (r : Rule) : Bool :=
  r.binderNames.eraseDups.length == r.binders.length &&
  r.binders.all (fun b => !b.name.isEmpty) &&
  !r.id.isEmpty &&
  r.usedAssumptions.all (r.assumptions.contains ·) &&
  r.usedIntentions.all (r.intentions.contains ·) &&
  r.intentions.all IntId.wellFormed &&
  r.operationalizations.all (fun o => !o.concepts.isEmpty && o.concepts.all fun c =>
    c.startsWith "drv." || Primitives.primitiveNames.contains (defName c) || knowsAtom (defName c))

/-- Structural well-formedness: at least one binder, and `wellFormedBody`. -/
def wellFormed (r : Rule) : Bool := !r.binders.isEmpty && r.wellFormedBody

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Static check
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- Variables in scope with their sorts, the innermost first. -/
abbrev Scope := List (String × EntityKind)

/-- Whether `v` is bound and its innermost binding has sort `k`, as evaluation's lookup reads it. -/
def Scope.binds (scope : Scope) (v : String) (k : EntityKind) : Bool :=
  (scope.find? (·.1 == v)).map (·.2) == some k

/-- Resolve arguments against the scope with dummy ids, checking each variable's sort against the
    position's expected sort when the table knows it. An entity position takes a variable only:
    a literal or a number there would name a track, region or device the rule has no right to. -/
private def dummyArgs (scope : Scope) (sorts : Option (List (Option EntityKind))) (args : List Arg)
    : Except String (List Primitives.DArg) :=
  (args.zip (List.range args.length)).mapM fun (a, k) =>
    match a with
    | .var v =>
      match scope.find? (·.1 == v) with
      | none => .error s!"variable `{v}` is not bound"
      | some (_, vs) =>
        match sorts.bind (·[k]?) with
        | some (some want) => if want == vs then .ok (.v 0) else .error s!"variable `{v}` has sort {repr vs}, position {k} wants {repr want}"
        | some none => .error s!"variable `{v}` where position {k} takes a literal"
        | none => .ok (.v 0)
    | .lit l =>
      match sorts.bind (·[k]?) with
      | some (some want) => .error s!"literal `{l}` where position {k} wants a {repr want}"
      | _ => .ok (.s l)
    | .nat n =>
      match sorts.bind (·[k]?) with
      | some (some want) => .error s!"number `{n}` where position {k} wants a {repr want}"
      | _ => .ok (.n n)

private def isMalformed : UnknownReason → Option String
  | .malformed w => some w
  | .parameterMissing w => some w
  | _ => none

private def emptyScene : Scene := { t := 0 }
private def emptyCtx : Primitives.Ctx := { scenes := #[], times := #[], ρ := {} }

/-- A quantifier's kind: a spelling the codec decodes. A variable is a concept's literal formal
    that reached the check unfilled. -/
private def kindErrors (where_ : String) (a : Arg) (what : String) (known : String → Bool) : List String :=
  match a with
  | .lit s => if known s then [] else [s!"{where_}: {what} kind `{s}` names no kind"]
  | .var v => [s!"{where_}: {what} kind `{v}` is a variable; spell the kind, or fill it from a literal formal"]
  | .nat _ => [s!"{where_}: {what} kind is a number"]

private def constParamErrors (where_ name : String) (ps : List Term) : List String :=
  ps.filter (!Term.isConstant ·) |>.map fun _ => s!"{where_}: `{name}` parameter is not a constant term"

/-- A heading change's step bound: a literal or a reading parameter, a literal strictly positive. -/
private def stepErrors (where_ : String) : Term → List String
  | .lit q _ => if Q.lt Q.zero q then [] else [s!"{where_}: heading_since step bound is not strictly positive"]
  | .param _ => []
  | _ => [s!"{where_}: heading_since step bound is not a literal or a reading parameter"]

mutual
  partial def checkTerm (scope : Scope) (where_ : String) : Term → List String
    | .lit _ _ | .param _ => []
    | .measure a args =>
      match dummyArgs scope (atomArgSorts a) args with
      | .error e => [s!"{where_}: {e}"]
      | .ok ds => match evalMeasure emptyScene a ds with
        | .error w => match isMalformed w with | some m => [s!"{where_}: measure `{a}`: {m}"] | none => []
        | .ok _ => []
    | .quantity concept args ps =>
      let inner := ps.flatMap (checkTerm scope where_) ++ constParamErrors where_ concept ps
      match dummyArgs scope (Primitives.argSorts concept) args with
      | .error e => [s!"{where_}: {e}"] ++ inner
      | .ok ds => match Primitives.evalQ concept emptyCtx ds (ps.map fun _ => Q.zero) with
        | .error w => (match isMalformed w with | some m => [s!"{where_}: `{concept}`: {m}"] | none => []) ++ inner
        | .ok _ => inner
    | .distanceWhile subj φ =>
      (if scope.binds subj .track then [] else [s!"{where_}: subject `{subj}` is not a bound track"]) ++
      checkFormula scope where_ φ
    | .sinceRise φ => checkFormula scope where_ φ
    | .headingSince subj g ψ =>
      (if scope.binds subj .track then [] else [s!"{where_}: subject `{subj}` is not a bound track"]) ++
      stepErrors where_ g ++ checkTerm scope where_ g ++ checkFormula scope where_ ψ
    | .aggregate _ v φ t => checkFormula ((v, .track) :: scope) where_ φ ++ checkTerm ((v, .track) :: scope) where_ t
    | .add a b | .sub a b | .mul a b | .div a b => checkTerm scope where_ a ++ checkTerm scope where_ b
    | .neg a | .abs a => checkTerm scope where_ a
    | .cond φ a b => checkFormula scope where_ φ ++ checkTerm scope where_ a ++ checkTerm scope where_ b

  partial def checkFormula (scope : Scope) (where_ : String) : Formula → List String
    | .tt | .ff | .asm _ => []
    | .intent _ who target =>
      [(who, EntityKind.track, "road user"), (target, EntityKind.region, "region")].flatMap fun (a, want, what) =>
        match a with
        | .var v => if scope.binds v want then [] else [s!"{where_}: intent's {what} `{v}` is not a bound {repr want}"]
        | _ => [s!"{where_}: intent's {what} is a variable"]
    | .same a b => [a, b].flatMap fun arg => match arg with
      | .var v => if scope.any (·.1 == v) then [] else [s!"{where_}: variable `{v}` is not bound"]
      | _ => [s!"{where_}: `same` compares two bound variables"]
    | .atom name args ps =>
      let inner := ps.flatMap (checkTerm scope where_) ++ constParamErrors where_ name ps
      match dummyArgs scope (atomArgSorts name) args with
      | .error e => [s!"{where_}: {e}"] ++ inner
      | .ok ds =>
        if name == "ru_aggregate" then inner     -- membership is the reading's; `checkReading` holds the word
        else match evalAtomE emptyScene name ds (ps.map fun _ => Q.zero) with
        | .error w => (match isMalformed w with | some m => [s!"{where_}: atom `{name}`: {m}"] | none => []) ++ inner
        | .ok _ => inner
    | .cmp l _ r => checkTerm scope where_ l ++ checkTerm scope where_ r
    | .not φ | .always φ | .eventually φ => checkFormula scope where_ φ
    | .and φ ψ | .or φ ψ | .implies φ ψ | .until φ ψ | .since φ ψ => checkFormula scope where_ φ ++ checkFormula scope where_ ψ
    | .holdsFor m d subj φ | .within m d subj φ =>
      windowErrors scope where_ m d subj ++ checkTerm scope where_ d ++ checkFormula scope where_ φ
    | .untilWithin m d subj φ ψ =>
      windowErrors scope where_ m d subj ++ checkTerm scope where_ d ++ checkFormula scope where_ φ ++ checkFormula scope where_ ψ
    | .atLast m d subj ψ φ =>
      windowErrors scope where_ m d subj ++ checkTerm scope where_ d ++ checkFormula scope where_ ψ ++ checkFormula scope where_ φ
    | .count e sφ _ _ => checkFormula scope where_ e ++ checkFormula scope where_ sφ
    | .rises φ => checkFormula scope where_ φ
    | .definedWhen p φ => checkFormula scope where_ p ++ checkFormula scope where_ φ
    | .derived concept args ps =>
      let inner := ps.flatMap (checkTerm scope where_) ++ constParamErrors where_ concept ps
      match dummyArgs scope (Primitives.argSorts concept) args with
      | .error e => [s!"{where_}: {e}"] ++ inner
      | .ok ds => match Primitives.evalB concept emptyCtx ds (ps.map fun _ => Q.zero) with
        | .error w => (match isMalformed w with | some m => [s!"{where_}: `{concept}`: {m}"] | none => []) ++ inner
        | .ok _ => inner
    | .rule _ map | .ruleApplies _ map => map.flatMap fun (_, outer) =>
        if scope.binds outer .track then [] else [s!"{where_}: composition maps to `{outer}`, not a bound track"]
    | .existsRegion k v φ | .forallRegion k v φ =>
      kindErrors where_ k "region" (fun s => (StructureKind.ofString s).isSome) ++ checkFormula ((v, .region) :: scope) where_ φ
    | .existsDevice k v φ | .forallDevice k v φ =>
      kindErrors where_ k "device" (fun s => (DeviceKind.ofString s).isSome) ++ checkFormula ((v, .device) :: scope) where_ φ
    | .existsUser v φ | .forallUser v φ => checkFormula ((v, .track) :: scope) where_ φ

  partial def windowErrors (scope : Scope) (where_ : String) (m : Measure) (d : Term) (subj : String) : List String :=
    (if m = .path && !scope.binds subj .track then [s!"{where_}: window subject `{subj}` is not a bound track"] else []) ++
    (if Term.isConstant d then [] else [s!"{where_}: window length is not a constant term"])
end

-- A declared intention read ahead of the judged observation: an `intent` leaf, or a composed
-- rule that reads one, within the scope of a future operator, in a formula or a term.
mutual
  partial def futureTerm (reads : String → Bool) (fut : Bool) : Term → List String
    | .quantity _ _ ps => ps.flatMap (futureTerm reads fut)
    | .distanceWhile _ φ | .sinceRise φ => futureReads reads fut φ
    | .headingSince _ g ψ => futureTerm reads fut g ++ futureReads reads fut ψ
    | .aggregate _ _ φ t => futureReads reads fut φ ++ futureTerm reads fut t
    | .add a b | .sub a b | .mul a b | .div a b => futureTerm reads fut a ++ futureTerm reads fut b
    | .neg a | .abs a => futureTerm reads fut a
    | .cond φ a b => futureReads reads fut φ ++ futureTerm reads fut a ++ futureTerm reads fut b
    | _ => []
  partial def futureReads (reads : String → Bool) (fut : Bool) : Formula → List String
    | .intent id _ _ => if fut then [s!"declared intention `{id}` is read ahead of the judged observation"] else []
    | .rule id _ | .ruleApplies id _ =>
      if fut && reads id then [s!"`{id}` reads a declared intention and is read ahead of the judged observation"] else []
    | .atom _ _ ps | .derived _ _ ps => ps.flatMap (futureTerm reads fut)
    | .cmp l _ r => futureTerm reads fut l ++ futureTerm reads fut r
    | .always φ | .eventually φ => futureReads reads true φ
    | .until φ ψ => futureReads reads true φ ++ futureReads reads true ψ
    | .within _ d _ φ => futureTerm reads fut d ++ futureReads reads true φ
    | .untilWithin _ d _ φ ψ => futureTerm reads fut d ++ futureReads reads true φ ++ futureReads reads true ψ
    | .not φ | .rises φ => futureReads reads fut φ
    | .and φ ψ | .or φ ψ | .implies φ ψ | .since φ ψ | .definedWhen φ ψ => futureReads reads fut φ ++ futureReads reads fut ψ
    | .holdsFor _ d _ φ => futureTerm reads fut d ++ futureReads reads fut φ
    | .atLast _ d _ ψ φ => futureTerm reads fut d ++ futureReads reads fut ψ ++ futureReads reads fut φ
    | .count e sφ _ _ => futureReads reads fut e ++ futureReads reads fut sφ
    | .existsRegion _ _ φ | .forallRegion _ _ φ | .existsDevice _ _ φ | .forallDevice _ _ φ
    | .existsUser _ φ | .forallUser _ φ => futureReads reads fut φ
    | _ => []
end

-- The distance travelled since the trace began (`kin_path_length`), whose zero is the start of the
-- recording, read where it can decide a search into the past: inside an operand of `since`, of
-- `atLast` or of `count`, inside the formula of `sinceRise`, the onset of `headingSince` or the
-- formula of `rises`, directly or through a composed rule that reads it. Everywhere else it is
-- ordinary arithmetic; path windows and `distanceWhile` measure differences and are never this.
mutual
  partial def pathTerm (reads : String → Bool) (back : Bool) : Term → List String
    | .measure "kin_path_length" _ =>
      if back then ["the distance travelled since the trace began (`kin_path_length`) is read inside a search into the past (`since`, `sinceRise`, `atLast`, `count` or `rises`); the start of a recording is no event of a road user's history"] else []
    | .quantity _ _ ps => ps.flatMap (pathTerm reads back)
    | .distanceWhile _ φ => pathReads reads back φ
    | .sinceRise φ => pathReads reads true φ
    | .headingSince _ g ψ => pathTerm reads back g ++ pathReads reads true ψ
    | .aggregate _ _ φ t => pathReads reads back φ ++ pathTerm reads back t
    | .add a b | .sub a b | .mul a b | .div a b => pathTerm reads back a ++ pathTerm reads back b
    | .neg a | .abs a => pathTerm reads back a
    | .cond φ a b => pathReads reads back φ ++ pathTerm reads back a ++ pathTerm reads back b
    | _ => []
  partial def pathReads (reads : String → Bool) (back : Bool) : Formula → List String
    | .rule id _ | .ruleApplies id _ =>
      if back && reads id then [s!"`{id}` reads the distance travelled since the trace began and is composed inside a search into the past"] else []
    | .atom _ _ ps | .derived _ _ ps => ps.flatMap (pathTerm reads back)
    | .cmp l _ r => pathTerm reads back l ++ pathTerm reads back r
    | .since φ ψ => pathReads reads true φ ++ pathReads reads true ψ
    | .atLast _ d _ ψ φ => pathTerm reads back d ++ pathReads reads true ψ ++ pathReads reads true φ
    | .count e sφ _ _ => pathReads reads true e ++ pathReads reads true sφ
    | .rises φ => pathReads reads true φ
    | .not φ | .always φ | .eventually φ => pathReads reads back φ
    | .and φ ψ | .or φ ψ | .implies φ ψ | .until φ ψ | .definedWhen φ ψ => pathReads reads back φ ++ pathReads reads back ψ
    | .holdsFor _ d _ φ | .within _ d _ φ => pathTerm reads back d ++ pathReads reads back φ
    | .untilWithin _ d _ φ ψ => pathTerm reads back d ++ pathReads reads back φ ++ pathReads reads back ψ
    | .existsRegion _ _ φ | .forallRegion _ _ φ | .existsDevice _ _ φ | .forallDevice _ _ φ
    | .existsUser _ φ | .forallUser _ φ => pathReads reads back φ
    | _ => []
end

/-- Whether a rule, or a rule it composes, reads `kin_path_length` anywhere. -/
def readsPath (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : Bool :=
  (closure rules r).any fun x => x.formulas.any fun φ => !(pathReads (fun _ => false) true φ).isEmpty

/-- Every defect a rule has before any trace; empty for a rule the evaluator will never report
    `malformed` or `unboundVariable` on: an empty id; no binder, or one unnamed or named twice;
    an assumption or intention read but not declared, or an intention id ill-formed; an
    operationalization bounded by nothing, or by a name that is no atom, primitive or concept; a
    name no table knows; an atom, measure, primitive or concept given the wrong number of
    arguments; an unbound variable, or one of the wrong sort where a track, region or device is
    read (such a position takes a variable, never a spelling or a number; a literal position
    takes no variable); a spelling no enumeration decodes; a quantifier kind that is not a
    spelling; a parameter of an atom or a call, or a window's length, that is not a constant
    term (a literal, a reading parameter, or arithmetic over them); a heading change's step bound
    that is not a literal or a reading parameter, or a literal one not strictly positive; a
    declared intention read ahead of the judged observation; the distance travelled since the trace began read inside a
    search into the past; a composed rule not in the set, or a map that names a variable not
    bound to a track, misses one of its binders or names one it does not have. `regions` names
    variables the caller binds to regions: the region formals of a concept's instance, which
    alone may then have no binder. -/
def check (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (regions : List String := []) : List String :=
  let scope : Scope := r.binderNames.map (fun n => (n, EntityKind.track)) ++ regions.map fun n => (n, EntityKind.region)
  let formed := if regions.isEmpty then r.wellFormed else r.wellFormedBody
  let reads (id : String) : Bool := match rules.find? (·.id == id) with
    | some r' => r'.readsIntention rules
    | none => false
  (if formed then [] else [s!"{r.id}: binders empty, duplicated or unnamed, an assumption, intention or concept undeclared, or an intention id ill-formed"]) ++
  (r.binders.flatMap fun b => checkFormula [(b.name, .track)] s!"{r.id} binder `{b.name}`" b.cls) ++
  checkFormula scope s!"{r.id} applicability" r.applicability ++
  checkFormula scope s!"{r.id} obligation" r.obligation ++
  (r.formulas.flatMap (futureReads reads false) |>.eraseDups.map fun e => s!"{r.id}: {e}") ++
  (r.formulas.flatMap (pathReads (fun id => (rules.find? (·.id == id)).any (readsPath rules)) false)
    |>.eraseDups.map fun e => s!"{r.id}: {e}") ++
  (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.compositions).flatMap (fun (id, map) =>
    match rules.find? (·.id == id) with
    | none => [s!"{r.id}: composes unknown rule `{id}`"]
    | some r' =>
      (map.filter (fun (inner, _) => !r'.binderNames.contains inner) |>.map fun (inner, _) => s!"{r.id}: composition of `{id}` maps `{inner}`, not one of its binders") ++
      (r'.binderNames.filter (fun b => !map.any (·.1 == b)) |>.map fun b => s!"{r.id}: composition of `{id}` leaves its binder `{b}` unmapped"))

/-- The aggregate ids `who` names that the reading does not declare, or whose declaration lists
    an id that is no road-user class. -/
def aggregateDefects (who : String) (ids : List String) (ρ : Reading) : List String :=
  ids.eraseDups.flatMap fun w =>
    match ρ.aggregate w with
    | none => [s!"{who}: aggregate `{w}` is not declared by the reading"]
    | some a => (a.included ++ a.unresolved).filter (fun id => !id.startsWith "ru." || (RoadUserClass.ofString (id.drop 3).toString).isNone)
        |>.map fun id => s!"{who}: aggregate `{w}` lists `{id}`, which is not a road-user class"

/-- Parameters and aggregates that the rule, or a rule it composes, names and the reading lacks,
    each rule read with its calls of the concepts `cs` expanded. -/
def checkReading (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (ρ : Reading) (cs : List Concept := []) : List String :=
  (Rule.closure rules r).flatMap fun x =>
    let xx := Concept.expandRule cs x
    (xx.params.filter (!ρ.has ·) |>.map fun p => s!"{x.id}: parameter `{p}` is not in the reading")
    ++ aggregateDefects x.id (xx.formulas.flatMap Formula.aggregateIds) ρ

end Rule

/-- Rule composition over a library, with fuel bounding the nesting depth. The composed rule's
    binders are bound through `map` (inner binder ↦ caller variable); an unmapped binder is an
    unbound variable, an unknown id is `compositionUnknown`. `engaged` selects the composed
    rule's applicability (for an exception or a condition) over its compliance. -/
def composeWith (rules : List Rule) (d : Primitives.Ctx) :
    Nat → String → List (String × String) → Binding → Bool → Array R
  | 0, id, _, _, _ => Array.replicate d.n (R.u (.compositionUnknown id))
  | fuel + 1, id, map, β, engaged =>
    match rules.find? (·.id == id) with
    | none => Array.replicate d.n (R.u (.compositionUnknown id))
    | some r =>
      let β' : Binding := ⟨map.filterMap fun (inner, outer) => (β.lookup outer).map fun v => (inner, v)⟩
      let c : Semantics.SemCtx := { d := d, β := β', compose := composeWith rules d fuel }
      if engaged then r.engagedAll c else r.asRAll c

/-- The evaluation context for a rule set over an indexed trace: composition resolves against
    `rules`, nested at most `rules.length` deep. -/
def Rule.context (rules : List Rule) (d : Primitives.Ctx) (β : Binding) : Semantics.SemCtx :=
  { d := d, β := β, compose := composeWith rules d rules.length }

namespace Concept
open Semantics

-- Every concept call against the callee's signature: a track formal takes a variable bound to a
-- track, a region formal one bound to a region, a literal formal one of its admissible values, a
-- nat formal a number. Run on formulas whose own literal and nat formals already hold values.
mutual
  partial def termCallDefects (cs : List Concept) (scope : Rule.Scope) (where_ : String) : Term → List String
    | .quantity n args ps => callArgs cs scope where_ n args ++ ps.flatMap (termCallDefects cs scope where_)
    | .measure _ _ | .lit _ _ | .param _ => []
    | .distanceWhile _ φ | .sinceRise φ => callDefects cs scope where_ φ
    | .headingSince _ g ψ => termCallDefects cs scope where_ g ++ callDefects cs scope where_ ψ
    | .aggregate _ v φ t => callDefects cs ((v, .track) :: scope) where_ φ ++ termCallDefects cs ((v, .track) :: scope) where_ t
    | .add a b | .sub a b | .mul a b | .div a b => termCallDefects cs scope where_ a ++ termCallDefects cs scope where_ b
    | .neg a | .abs a => termCallDefects cs scope where_ a
    | .cond φ a b => callDefects cs scope where_ φ ++ termCallDefects cs scope where_ a ++ termCallDefects cs scope where_ b
  partial def callDefects (cs : List Concept) (scope : Rule.Scope) (where_ : String) : Formula → List String
    | .derived n args ps => callArgs cs scope where_ n args ++ ps.flatMap (termCallDefects cs scope where_)
    | .atom _ _ ps => ps.flatMap (termCallDefects cs scope where_)
    | .cmp l _ r => termCallDefects cs scope where_ l ++ termCallDefects cs scope where_ r
    | .not φ | .always φ | .eventually φ | .rises φ => callDefects cs scope where_ φ
    | .and φ ψ | .or φ ψ | .implies φ ψ | .until φ ψ | .since φ ψ | .definedWhen φ ψ | .count φ ψ _ _ =>
      callDefects cs scope where_ φ ++ callDefects cs scope where_ ψ
    | .holdsFor _ d _ φ | .within _ d _ φ => termCallDefects cs scope where_ d ++ callDefects cs scope where_ φ
    | .untilWithin _ d _ φ ψ | .atLast _ d _ φ ψ =>
      termCallDefects cs scope where_ d ++ callDefects cs scope where_ φ ++ callDefects cs scope where_ ψ
    | .existsUser v φ | .forallUser v φ => callDefects cs ((v, .track) :: scope) where_ φ
    | .existsRegion _ v φ | .forallRegion _ v φ => callDefects cs ((v, .region) :: scope) where_ φ
    | .existsDevice _ v φ | .forallDevice _ v φ => callDefects cs ((v, .device) :: scope) where_ φ
    | _ => []
  partial def callArgs (cs : List Concept) (scope : Rule.Scope) (where_ name : String) (args : List Arg) : List String :=
    match cs.find? (·.leanName == name) with
    | none => []
    | some c =>
      if args.length != c.args.length then []        -- an arity the expansion leaves for `Rule.check` to report
      else (c.args.zip args).filterMap fun ((n, so), a) =>
        let bad := some s!"{where_}: `{c.id}` formal `{n}` ({repr so}) is given {repr a}"
        match so, a with
        | .track, .var v => if scope.binds v .track then none else bad
        | .region, .var v => if scope.binds v .region then none else bad
        | .literal vs, .lit l => if vs.contains l then none else bad
        | .nat, .nat _ => none
        | _, _ => bad
end

/-- `callDefects` on a rule before expansion: each binder's class with that binder, the
    applicability and the obligation with every binder, all as tracks. -/
def ruleCallDefects (cs : List Concept) (r : Rule) : List String :=
  let scope : Rule.Scope := r.binderNames.map fun n => (n, EntityKind.track)
  (r.binders.flatMap fun b => callDefects cs [(b.name, .track)] s!"{r.id} binder `{b.name}`" b.cls) ++
  callDefects cs scope s!"{r.id} applicability" r.applicability ++
  callDefects cs scope s!"{r.id} obligation" r.obligation


/-- Every defect a concept has before any trace: an empty id; a formal or a parameter named
    twice; a parameter named as a reading's, or a body parameter that is no formal parameter; a
    literal formal that admits no value; a composed rule or a declared intention in the body (a
    concept reads neither); a referenced concept unknown, or a reference cycle; and, on every
    admissible instantiation of its literal formals with its calls expanded, every defect
    `Rule.check` finds in a formula and a call whose arguments do not fit the callee's formals. -/
def check (cs : List Concept) (c : Concept) : List String :=
  let names := c.args.map (·.1)
  let pnames := c.paramNames
  let body := c.bodyFormula
  let structural :=
    (if c.id.isEmpty then ["concept: empty id"] else []) ++
    (if names.eraseDups.length != names.length then [s!"{c.id}: duplicate formal argument"] else []) ++
    (if pnames.eraseDups.length != pnames.length then [s!"{c.id}: duplicate formal parameter"] else []) ++
    (pnames.filter (·.contains '.') |>.map fun p => s!"{c.id}: parameter `{p}` names a reading parameter; a body references its formals only") ++
    (c.args.filterMap fun (n, s) => match s with
      | .literal [] => some s!"{c.id}: literal formal `{n}` admits no value"
      | _ => none) ++
    ((Formula.params body).eraseDups.filter (!pnames.contains ·) |>.map fun p => s!"{c.id}: `{p}` is not a formal parameter") ++
    ((Formula.composed body).map fun id => s!"{c.id}: a concept composes no rule (`{id}`)") ++
    ((Formula.intentions body).eraseDups.map fun id => s!"{c.id}: a concept reads no declared intention (`{id}`)") ++
    (c.refs.filter (fun n => !cs.any (·.leanName == n))
      |>.map fun n => s!"{c.id}: references unknown concept `{n}`") ++
    (if (onCycle cs).contains c.id then [s!"{c.id}: on a reference cycle"] else [])
  let scope : Rule.Scope := c.args.filterMap fun (n, s) => match s with
    | .track => some (n, EntityKind.track)
    | .region => some (n, EntityKind.region)
    | _ => none
  let ps : List Term := c.params.map fun p => Term.param p.name
  let byInstance := (samples c).flatMap fun args =>
    match instantiate c args ps "check" with
    | none => [s!"{c.id}: arity"]
    | some b =>
      let φ := match b with | .formula φ => φ | .quantity t => Formula.cmp t .eq t
      let φx := expand cs φ
      callDefects cs scope c.id φ ++ Rule.checkFormula scope c.id φx ++
        (Rule.pathReads (fun _ => false) false φx).map fun e => s!"{c.id}: {e}"
  structural ++ byInstance.eraseDups

/-- The aggregates a concept's body names, its calls expanded, that the reading does not declare
    or declares with an id that is no road-user class. -/
def checkReading (cs : List Concept) (c : Concept) (ρ : Reading) : List String :=
  Rule.aggregateDefects c.id (aggregateIds cs c) ρ

end Concept

end TrafficSpec

1	/-
2	  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Monitor
3	  The report: one row per rule and grounding, with support, episode verdict, timeline, the
4	  histogram of unknown reasons, residues and the surrogate flag; rendered as tab-separated text
5	  (the gate's contract) and as JSON lines (the diagnosis tooling's).
6	
7	  It composes everything below it and owns nothing else. The row format is a contract with
8	  `tools/check_spec.py` and `scripts/diagnostics/`; changing a line here is a cross-artifact change.
9	  Surrogate rows never enter the concrete tallies.
10	
11	  Text format (tab-separated; one record per line):
12	    SOURCE   source  instants=N  gap=<seconds>
13	    RULE     rule  concrete|surrogate  support  absent-ids(,)  groundings=N  live=bool  v=N c=N na=N u=N
14	    GROUND   rule  grounding  episode
15	    TL       rule  grounding  t_from  t_to  verdict            (runs of equal verdict, ms timestamps)
16	    UNK      rule  grounding  reason  count
17	    RESIDUE  rule  text
18	    SUMMARY  concrete|surrogate  rules=N supported=N partial=N unsupported=N live=N v=N c=N na=N u=N
19	-/
20	import Lean.Data.Json
21	import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Grounding
22	import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Manifest
23	
24	namespace TrafficSpec
25	namespace Monitor
26	open Grounding
27	
28	structure Row where
29	  rule : String
30	  surrogate : Bool
31	  support : Support
32	  grounding : Grounding
33	  episode : Verdict
34	  timeline : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)
35	  unknowns : List (String × Nat)
36	  residues : List String
37	  deriving Repr, Inhabited
38	
39	structure RuleLine where
40	  rule : String
41	  surrogate : Bool
42	  support : Support
43	  groundings : Nat
44	  live : Bool
45	  violated : Nat
46	  compliant : Nat
47	  notApplicable : Nat
48	  unknown : Nat
49	  deriving Repr, Inhabited
50	
51	structure Report where
52	  source : String
53	  instants : Nat
54	  gap : Q
55	  rules : List RuleLine
56	  rows : List Row
57	  deriving Repr, Inhabited
58	
59	def histogram (tl : List Verdict) : List (String × Nat) :=
60	  let tags := tl.flatMap fun v => (v.reasons.map UnknownReason.tag).eraseDups
61	  tags.eraseDups.map fun t => (t, tags.count t)
62	
63	def countVerdict (vs : List Verdict) (p : Verdict → Bool) : Nat := (vs.filter p).length
64	def isUnknown : Verdict → Bool | .unknown _ => true | _ => false
65	
66	/-- Evaluate a rule set over one trace as the source would have produced it, the rules' concept
67	    calls expanded over `cs`. Unsupported rules are reported without groundings: nothing they
68	    say could be decided. A trace the admission rejects is not evaluated: its defects are returned. -/
69	def check (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (m : Manifest) (cs : List Concept := []) : Except (List String) Report := do
70	  let rules := rules.map (Concept.expandRule cs)
71	  let S ← Setup.admit rules (maskTrace m τ) ρ m.reidGap
72	  let per := rules.map fun r =>
73	    let sup := support rules r m
74	    match sup with
75	    | .unsupported _ => ({ rule := r.id, surrogate := r.surrogate, support := sup, groundings := 0, live := false,
76	                           violated := 0, compliant := 0, notApplicable := 0, unknown := 0 : RuleLine }, ([] : List Row))
77	    | _ =>
78	      let evaluated : List (Grounding × Grounding.Timeline × Verdict) := Grounding.check S r

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Monitor
  The report: one row per rule and grounding, with support, episode verdict, timeline, the
  histogram of unknown reasons, residues and the surrogate flag; rendered as tab-separated text
  (the gate's contract) and as JSON lines (the diagnosis tooling's).

  It composes everything below it and owns nothing else. The row format is a contract with
  `tools/check_spec.py` and `scripts/diagnostics/`; changing a line here is a cross-artifact change.
  Surrogate rows never enter the concrete tallies.

  Text format (tab-separated; one record per line):
    SOURCE   source  instants=N  gap=<seconds>
    RULE     rule  concrete|surrogate  support  absent-ids(,)  groundings=N  live=bool  v=N c=N na=N u=N
    GROUND   rule  grounding  episode
    TL       rule  grounding  t_from  t_to  verdict            (runs of equal verdict, ms timestamps)
    UNK      rule  grounding  reason  count
    RESIDUE  rule  text
    SUMMARY  concrete|surrogate  rules=N supported=N partial=N unsupported=N live=N v=N c=N na=N u=N
-/
import Lean.Data.Json
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Grounding
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Manifest

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Monitor
open Grounding

structure Row where
  rule : String
  surrogate : Bool
  support : Support
  grounding : Grounding
  episode : Verdict
  timeline : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)
  unknowns : List (String × Nat)
  residues : List String
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

structure RuleLine where
  rule : String
  surrogate : Bool
  support : Support
  groundings : Nat
  live : Bool
  violated : Nat
  compliant : Nat
  notApplicable : Nat
  unknown : Nat
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

structure Report where
  source : String
  instants : Nat
  gap : Q
  rules : List RuleLine
  rows : List Row
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

def histogram (tl : List Verdict) : List (String × Nat) :=
  let tags := tl.flatMap fun v => (v.reasons.map UnknownReason.tag).eraseDups
  tags.eraseDups.map fun t => (t, tags.count t)

def countVerdict (vs : List Verdict) (p : Verdict → Bool) : Nat := (vs.filter p).length
def isUnknown : Verdict → Bool | .unknown _ => true | _ => false

/-- Evaluate a rule set over one trace as the source would have produced it, the rules' concept
    calls expanded over `cs`. Unsupported rules are reported without groundings: nothing they
    say could be decided. A trace the admission rejects is not evaluated: its defects are returned. -/
def check (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (m : Manifest) (cs : List Concept := []) : Except (List String) Report := do
  let rules := rules.map (Concept.expandRule cs)
  let S ← Setup.admit rules (maskTrace m τ) ρ m.reidGap
  let per := rules.map fun r =>
    let sup := support rules r m
    match sup with
    | .unsupported _ => ({ rule := r.id, surrogate := r.surrogate, support := sup, groundings := 0, live := false,
                           violated := 0, compliant := 0, notApplicable := 0, unknown := 0 : RuleLine }, ([] : List Row))
    | _ =>
      let evaluated : List (Grounding × Grounding.Timeline × Verdict) := Grounding.check S r
      let rows : List Row := evaluated.map fun (e : Grounding × Grounding.Timeline × Verdict) =>
        let g := e.1; let tl := e.2.1; let ep := e.2.2
        let vs : List Verdict := tl.verdicts.toList.map Prod.snd
        { rule := r.id, surrogate := r.surrogate, support := sup, grounding := g, episode := ep,
          timeline := tl.verdicts, unknowns := histogram vs, residues := r.residues }
      let eps : List Verdict := rows.map Row.episode
      ({ rule := r.id, surrogate := r.surrogate, support := sup, groundings := rows.length,
         live := evaluated.any (fun e => e.2.1.live),
         violated := countVerdict eps (· == Verdict.violated), compliant := countVerdict eps (· == Verdict.compliant),
         notApplicable := countVerdict eps (· == Verdict.notApplicable), unknown := countVerdict eps isUnknown : RuleLine }, rows)
  pure { source := m.source, instants := τ.length, gap := m.reidGap, rules := per.map (·.1), rows := per.flatMap (·.2) }

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Text
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def qText (q : Q) : String :=
  let g := Nat.gcd q.num.natAbs q.den
  let g := if g == 0 then 1 else g
  let n := q.num / (Int.ofNat g)
  let d := q.den / g
  if d == 1 then toString n else s!"{n}/{d}"
def tabs (xs : List String) : String := String.intercalate "\t" xs
def kind (surrogate : Bool) : String := if surrogate then "surrogate" else "concrete"

/-- Runs of equal verdicts: (from, to, verdict). -/
def runs (tl : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)) : List (Timestamp × Timestamp × Verdict) :=
  tl.toList.foldl (fun acc (t, v) =>
    match acc with
    | (a, _, v') :: rest => if v' == v then (a, t, v) :: rest else (t, t, v) :: acc
    | [] => [(t, t, v)]) [] |>.reverse

def rowLines (row : Row) : List String :=
  let g := row.grounding.render
  [tabs ["GROUND", row.rule, g, row.episode.tag]] ++
  ((runs row.timeline).map fun (a, b', v) => tabs ["TL", row.rule, g, toString a, toString b', v.tag]) ++
  (row.unknowns.map fun (t, n) => tabs ["UNK", row.rule, g, t, toString n])

def ruleLine (l : RuleLine) : String :=
  tabs ["RULE", l.rule, kind l.surrogate, l.support.tag, String.intercalate "," l.support.absent,
        s!"groundings={l.groundings}", s!"live={l.live}",
        s!"v={l.violated}", s!"c={l.compliant}", s!"na={l.notApplicable}", s!"u={l.unknown}"]

def summaryLine (surrogate : Bool) (ls : List RuleLine) : String :=
  let ls := ls.filter (·.surrogate == surrogate)
  let n (p : RuleLine → Bool) := (ls.filter p).length
  let sum (f : RuleLine → Nat) := ls.foldl (fun a l => a + f l) 0
  tabs ["SUMMARY", kind surrogate, s!"rules={ls.length}",
        s!"supported={n (·.support == .supported)}",
        s!"partial={n fun l => match l.support with | .partially _ => true | _ => false}",
        s!"unsupported={n fun l => match l.support with | .unsupported _ => true | _ => false}",
        s!"live={n (·.live)}", s!"v={sum (·.violated)}", s!"c={sum (·.compliant)}",
        s!"na={sum (·.notApplicable)}", s!"u={sum (·.unknown)}"]

def renderText (rep : Report) : String :=
  let header := tabs ["SOURCE", rep.source, s!"instants={rep.instants}", s!"gap={qText rep.gap}"]
  let ruleBlocks := rep.rules.flatMap fun l =>
    let residues : List String := ((rep.rows.find? (·.rule == l.rule)).map (·.residues)).getD []
    [ruleLine l] ++
    (rep.rows.filter (·.rule == l.rule)).flatMap rowLines ++
    residues.map fun t => tabs ["RESIDUE", l.rule, t]
  String.intercalate "\n" ([header] ++ ruleBlocks ++ [summaryLine false rep.rules, summaryLine true rep.rules]) ++ "\n"

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- JSON lines
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
open Lean in
def verdictJson (v : Verdict) : Json :=
  Json.mkObj [("verdict", v.tag), ("reasons", Json.arr (v.reasons.map fun r => Json.str r.tag).toArray)]

open Lean in
def rowJson (row : Row) : Json :=
  Json.mkObj [
    ("kind", "grounding"), ("rule", row.rule), ("surrogate", row.surrogate), ("support", row.support.tag),
    ("grounding", Json.mkObj (row.grounding.assign.map fun (n, t) => (n, Json.num t))),
    ("episode", verdictJson row.episode),
    ("timeline", Json.arr ((runs row.timeline).map fun (a, b', v) =>
        Json.mkObj [("from", Json.num a), ("to", Json.num b'), ("verdict", v.tag)]).toArray),
    ("unknowns", Json.mkObj (row.unknowns.map fun (t, n) => (t, Json.num n))),
    ("residues", Json.arr (row.residues.map Json.str).toArray)]

open Lean in
def ruleJson (l : RuleLine) : Json :=
  Json.mkObj [
    ("kind", "rule"), ("rule", l.rule), ("surrogate", l.surrogate), ("support", l.support.tag),
    ("absent", Json.arr (l.support.absent.map Json.str).toArray), ("groundings", Json.num l.groundings),
    ("live", l.live), ("violated", Json.num l.violated), ("compliant", Json.num l.compliant),
    ("not_applicable", Json.num l.notApplicable), ("unknown", Json.num l.unknown)]

open Lean in
def renderJsonLines (rep : Report) : String :=
  let header := Json.mkObj [("kind", "source"), ("source", rep.source), ("instants", Json.num rep.instants), ("gap", qText rep.gap)]
  String.intercalate "\n" ((header :: rep.rules.map ruleJson ++ rep.rows.map rowJson).map (·.compress)) ++ "\n"

end Monitor
end TrafficSpec

1	/-
2	  TRAINING SPLIT variant, generated by harness/tools/split.py from the full file: the lines that read the
3	  atoms the split omits are removed. Do not edit; regenerate.

5	/-
6	  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Grounding
7	  Which assignments of tracks to binders exist over a trace, how a broken track is followed, and
8	  the per-grounding timeline of verdicts.
9	
10	  A track is a source's identity, not an object's. When a tracker breaks and the adapter claims a
11	  continuation (`Scene.links`, old ↦ new), the trace is rewritten once to canonical identities
12	  when the break is shorter than the manifest's re-identification gap; the instants inside the gap
13	  are unknown (identityGap), never a fresh party. A binder whose track is not present at an
14	  instant outside any gap leaves the rule not engaged there: the other party has left the scene.
15	
16	  Groundings are tuples of distinct candidates that are co-present at some instant; each
17	  grounding evaluates the rule once over the whole trace, and formulas that depend on a subset of
18	  the binders are shared across the groundings that agree on that subset.
19	
20	  Rules never import this file: a rule that could see the census of tracks could special-case it.
21	-/
22	import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.RuleEval
23	import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Admission
24	
25	namespace TrafficSpec
26	namespace Grounding
27	open Semantics
28	
29	/-- An assignment of canonical tracks to binder names, and of regions to the variables a
30	    concept's instance takes as region formals (a rule's groundings bind none). -/
31	structure Grounding where
32	  assign : List (String × TrackId)
33	  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []
34	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
35	
36	def Grounding.render (g : Grounding) : String :=
37	  String.intercalate "," (g.assign.map fun (n, t) => s!"{n}={t}")
38	def Grounding.binding (g : Grounding) : Binding :=
39	  ⟨g.assign.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Val.track t)) ++ g.regions.map fun (n, r) => (n, Val.region r)⟩
40	
41	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
42	-- Identity: canonical tracks through accepted links, applied to the trace once
43	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
44	/-- The scene with every track id replaced by its canonical identity. -/
45	def canonicalScene (cm : List (TrackId × TrackId)) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
46	  let c := canon cm
47	  { s with
48	    subject := s.subject.map c
49	    users := s.users.map fun u => { u with track := c u.track }
50	    occupancyObserved := s.occupancyObserved.map c
51	    occupies := s.occupies.map fun (t, r) => (c t, r)
52	    relations := s.relations.map fun m => { m with a := c m.a, b := c m.b }
53	    intents := s.intents.map fun d => { d with vehicle := c d.vehicle } }
54	
55	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
56	-- Setup: the canonical, indexed trace and the rule set
57	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
58	structure Setup where
59	  rules : List Rule
60	  d : Primitives.Ctx
61	  gap : Q
62	  cm : List (TrackId × TrackId) := []
63	
64	def Setup.mk' (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Setup :=
65	  let arr := τ.toArray
66	  let cm := canonMap arr gap
67	  { rules := rules, d := Primitives.Ctx.mk' (τ.map (canonicalScene cm)) ρ, gap := gap, cm := cm }
68	
69	/-- The setup of a trace every evaluation reaches: built only when `Admission.defects` finds no
70	    defect in the trace as written, else the defects. -/
71	def Setup.admit (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Except (List String) Setup :=
72	  match Admission.defects τ gap with
73	  | [] => .ok (Setup.mk' rules τ ρ gap)
74	  | ds => .error ds
75	
76	def Setup.n (S : Setup) : Nat := S.d.n
77	def Setup.scenes (S : Setup) : Array Scene := S.d.scenes
78	def Setup.ctx (S : Setup) (β : Binding) : SemCtx := Rule.context S.rules S.d β
79	def Setup.tracks (S : Setup) : List TrackId := (S.scenes.toList.flatMap (·.tracks)).eraseDups
80	/-- First and last instant at which a canonical identity is present. -/
81	def Setup.span (S : Setup) (t : TrackId) : Option (Nat × Nat) :=
82	  match firstSeen S.scenes t, lastSeen S.scenes t with
83	  | some a, some b => some (a, b)
84	  | _, _ => none
85	
86	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
87	-- Enumeration
88	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
89	/-- Tracks that satisfy a binder's class at some instant (evaluated once per track). -/
90	def candidates (S : Setup) (b : Binder) : List TrackId :=
91	  S.tracks.filter fun t =>
92	    (Rule.evalRuleFormula (S.ctx ⟨[(b.name, .track t)]⟩) b.cls).any fun r => r.v == .t
93	
94	def spansOverlap (S : Setup) (a b : TrackId) : Bool :=
95	  match S.span a, S.span b with
96	  | some (a0, a1), some (b0, b1) => a0 ≤ b1 && b0 ≤ a1
97	  | _, _ => false
98	
99	/-- All assignments of distinct, pairwise co-present candidates to the binders, subject first.
100	    Each binder's candidates are computed once. -/
101	def groundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List Grounding :=
102	  let cands := r.binders.map fun b => (b.name, candidates S b)
103	  let rec go (bs : List (String × List TrackId)) (used : List TrackId) : List (List (String × TrackId)) :=
104	    match bs with
105	    | [] => [[]]
106	    | (name, cs) :: rest =>
107	      cs.filter (fun c => !used.contains c && used.all (spansOverlap S c)) |>.flatMap fun c =>
108	        (go rest (c :: used)).map fun tail => (name, c) :: tail
109	  (go cands []).map fun a => { assign := a }
110	
111	/-- Predicted grounding count without enumerating: the product of candidate counts (an upper
112	    bound when candidates overlap). -/
113	def predictedGroundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Nat :=
114	  r.binders.foldl (fun acc b => acc * (candidates S b).length) 1
115	
116	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
117	-- Timelines
118	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
119	/-- One evaluation of a rule for a grounding: the verdict per instant, whether the rule was
120	    engaged at some instant with every party present, and whether every party was present at
121	    some instant at all. -/
122	structure Timeline where
123	  verdicts : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)
124	  live : Bool
125	  present : Bool
126	  deriving Repr
127	
128	/-- Evaluate a rule for a grounding once. A binder absent inside its identity's span is an
129	    identity gap (unknown); absent outside it, the rule is not engaged. -/
130	def evaluate (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Timeline :=
131	  let c := S.ctx g.binding
132	  let engaged := r.engagedAll c
133	  let obl := Rule.evalRuleFormula c r.obligation
134	  let spans := g.assign.map fun (_, t) => (t, S.span t)
135	  let rows := (Array.range S.n).map fun i =>
136	    let s := S.scenes[i]!
137	    let missing := spans.filter fun (t, _) => !s.tracks.contains t
138	    let v : Verdict :=
139	      if missing.isEmpty then verdictAt engaged[i]! obl[i]!
140	      else
141	        let inGap := missing.filter fun (_, sp) => match sp with
142	          | some (a, b) => a < i && i < b
143	          | none => false
144	        if inGap.isEmpty then .notApplicable
145	        else .unknown (inGap.map fun (t, _) => .identityGap t)
146	    (s.t, v, missing.isEmpty && engaged[i]!.v == .t, missing.isEmpty)
147	  ⟨rows.map fun (t, v, _, _) => (t, v), rows.any fun (_, _, l, _) => l, rows.any fun (_, _, _, p) => p⟩
148	
149	def timeline (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Array (Timestamp × Verdict) := (evaluate S r g).verdicts
150	
151	/-- The verdict of a grounding at one instant. -/
152	def verdictAt (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) (i : Nat) : Verdict :=
153	  ((timeline S r g)[i]?).map (·.2) |>.getD (.unknown [.outOfRange])
154	
155	/-- The episode verdict: a violation anywhere is a violation; else any unknown is unknown (with
156	    every reason); else engaged anywhere is compliant; else not applicable. -/
157	def episode (tl : List Verdict) : Verdict :=
158	  if tl.any (· == .violated) then .violated
159	  else
160	    let unknowns := tl.flatMap Verdict.reasons
161	    if tl.any (fun v => match v with | .unknown _ => true | _ => false) then .unknown unknowns.eraseDups
162	    else if tl.any (· == .compliant) then .compliant
163	    else .notApplicable
164	
165	/-- Every grounding evaluated once: its episode verdict and timeline. -/
166	def check (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List (Grounding × Timeline × Verdict) :=
167	  (groundings S r).map fun g =>
168	    let tl := evaluate S r g
169	    (g, tl, episode (tl.verdicts.toList.map (·.2)))
170	
171	/-- Engaged (applicability true) at some instant for some grounding: the rule says something on
172	    this trace. -/
173	def live (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Bool := (check S r).any fun (_, tl, _) => tl.live
174	
175	end Grounding
176	end TrafficSpec

  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Grounding
  Which assignments of tracks to binders exist over a trace, how a broken track is followed, and
  the per-grounding timeline of verdicts.

  A track is a source's identity, not an object's. When a tracker breaks and the adapter claims a
  continuation (`Scene.links`, old ↦ new), the trace is rewritten once to canonical identities
  when the break is shorter than the manifest's re-identification gap; the instants inside the gap
  are unknown (identityGap), never a fresh party. A binder whose track is not present at an
  instant outside any gap leaves the rule not engaged there: the other party has left the scene.

  Groundings are tuples of distinct candidates that are co-present at some instant; each
  grounding evaluates the rule once over the whole trace, and formulas that depend on a subset of
  the binders are shared across the groundings that agree on that subset.

  Rules never import this file: a rule that could see the census of tracks could special-case it.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.RuleEval
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Admission

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Grounding
open Semantics

/-- An assignment of canonical tracks to binder names, and of regions to the variables a
    concept's instance takes as region formals (a rule's groundings bind none). -/
structure Grounding where
  assign : List (String × TrackId)
  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

def Grounding.render (g : Grounding) : String :=
  String.intercalate "," (g.assign.map fun (n, t) => s!"{n}={t}")
def Grounding.binding (g : Grounding) : Binding :=
  ⟨g.assign.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Val.track t)) ++ g.regions.map fun (n, r) => (n, Val.region r)⟩

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Identity: canonical tracks through accepted links, applied to the trace once
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- The scene with every track id replaced by its canonical identity. -/
def canonicalScene (cm : List (TrackId × TrackId)) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
  let c := canon cm
  { s with
    subject := s.subject.map c
    users := s.users.map fun u => { u with track := c u.track }
    occupancyObserved := s.occupancyObserved.map c
    occupies := s.occupies.map fun (t, r) => (c t, r)
    relations := s.relations.map fun m => { m with a := c m.a, b := c m.b }
    intents := s.intents.map fun d => { d with vehicle := c d.vehicle } }

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Setup: the canonical, indexed trace and the rule set
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
structure Setup where
  rules : List Rule
  d : Primitives.Ctx
  gap : Q
  cm : List (TrackId × TrackId) := []

def Setup.mk' (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Setup :=
  let arr := τ.toArray
  let cm := canonMap arr gap
  { rules := rules, d := Primitives.Ctx.mk' (τ.map (canonicalScene cm)) ρ, gap := gap, cm := cm }

/-- The setup of a trace every evaluation reaches: built only when `Admission.defects` finds no
    defect in the trace as written, else the defects. -/
def Setup.admit (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Except (List String) Setup :=
  match Admission.defects τ gap with
  | [] => .ok (Setup.mk' rules τ ρ gap)
  | ds => .error ds

def Setup.n (S : Setup) : Nat := S.d.n
def Setup.scenes (S : Setup) : Array Scene := S.d.scenes
def Setup.ctx (S : Setup) (β : Binding) : SemCtx := Rule.context S.rules S.d β
def Setup.tracks (S : Setup) : List TrackId := (S.scenes.toList.flatMap (·.tracks)).eraseDups
/-- First and last instant at which a canonical identity is present. -/
def Setup.span (S : Setup) (t : TrackId) : Option (Nat × Nat) :=
  match firstSeen S.scenes t, lastSeen S.scenes t with
  | some a, some b => some (a, b)
  | _, _ => none

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Enumeration
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- Tracks that satisfy a binder's class at some instant (evaluated once per track). -/
def candidates (S : Setup) (b : Binder) : List TrackId :=
  S.tracks.filter fun t =>
    (Rule.evalRuleFormula (S.ctx ⟨[(b.name, .track t)]⟩) b.cls).any fun r => r.v == .t

def spansOverlap (S : Setup) (a b : TrackId) : Bool :=
  match S.span a, S.span b with
  | some (a0, a1), some (b0, b1) => a0 ≤ b1 && b0 ≤ a1
  | _, _ => false

/-- All assignments of distinct, pairwise co-present candidates to the binders, subject first.
    Each binder's candidates are computed once. -/
def groundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List Grounding :=
  let cands := r.binders.map fun b => (b.name, candidates S b)
  let rec go (bs : List (String × List TrackId)) (used : List TrackId) : List (List (String × TrackId)) :=
    match bs with
    | [] => [[]]
    | (name, cs) :: rest =>
      cs.filter (fun c => !used.contains c && used.all (spansOverlap S c)) |>.flatMap fun c =>
        (go rest (c :: used)).map fun tail => (name, c) :: tail
  (go cands []).map fun a => { assign := a }

/-- Predicted grounding count without enumerating: the product of candidate counts (an upper
    bound when candidates overlap). -/
def predictedGroundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Nat :=
  r.binders.foldl (fun acc b => acc * (candidates S b).length) 1

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Timelines
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- One evaluation of a rule for a grounding: the verdict per instant, whether the rule was
    engaged at some instant with every party present, and whether every party was present at
    some instant at all. -/
structure Timeline where
  verdicts : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)
  live : Bool
  present : Bool
  deriving Repr

/-- Evaluate a rule for a grounding once. A binder absent inside its identity's span is an
    identity gap (unknown); absent outside it, the rule is not engaged. -/
def evaluate (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Timeline :=
  let c := S.ctx g.binding
  let engaged := r.engagedAll c
  let obl := Rule.evalRuleFormula c r.obligation
  let spans := g.assign.map fun (_, t) => (t, S.span t)
  let rows := (Array.range S.n).map fun i =>
    let s := S.scenes[i]!
    let missing := spans.filter fun (t, _) => !s.tracks.contains t
    let v : Verdict :=
      if missing.isEmpty then verdictAt engaged[i]! obl[i]!
      else
        let inGap := missing.filter fun (_, sp) => match sp with
          | some (a, b) => a < i && i < b
          | none => false
        if inGap.isEmpty then .notApplicable
        else .unknown (inGap.map fun (t, _) => .identityGap t)
    (s.t, v, missing.isEmpty && engaged[i]!.v == .t, missing.isEmpty)
  ⟨rows.map fun (t, v, _, _) => (t, v), rows.any fun (_, _, l, _) => l, rows.any fun (_, _, _, p) => p⟩

def timeline (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Array (Timestamp × Verdict) := (evaluate S r g).verdicts

/-- The verdict of a grounding at one instant. -/
def verdictAt (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) (i : Nat) : Verdict :=
  ((timeline S r g)[i]?).map (·.2) |>.getD (.unknown [.outOfRange])

/-- The episode verdict: a violation anywhere is a violation; else any unknown is unknown (with
    every reason); else engaged anywhere is compliant; else not applicable. -/
def episode (tl : List Verdict) : Verdict :=
  if tl.any (· == .violated) then .violated
  else
    let unknowns := tl.flatMap Verdict.reasons
    if tl.any (fun v => match v with | .unknown _ => true | _ => false) then .unknown unknowns.eraseDups
    else if tl.any (· == .compliant) then .compliant
    else .notApplicable

/-- Every grounding evaluated once: its episode verdict and timeline. -/
def check (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List (Grounding × Timeline × Verdict) :=
  (groundings S r).map fun g =>
    let tl := evaluate S r g
    (g, tl, episode (tl.verdicts.toList.map (·.2)))

/-- Engaged (applicability true) at some instant for some grounding: the rule says something on
    this trace. -/
def live (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Bool := (check S r).any fun (_, tl, _) => tl.live

end Grounding
end TrafficSpec

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Admission
  What a trace must satisfy, as written, before any rule is evaluated on it: the declared facts
  (assumptions and intentions) name what their scene holds, each once, by well-formed ids; no
  structure is labelled with an abstract kind or lists one among the kinds its source cannot tell
  (an abstract kind is the union of the kinds refining it, read only by a formula); and the
  accepted re-identification links are one-to-one.

  The checks are exact and read no geometry, so a recorded trace, a JSON case and a Lean witness
  are held to them alike. `Grounding.Setup.admit` calls them; every evaluation builds its setup
  there.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Identity
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Assumptions
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Intentions

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Admission

private def duplicates {α : Type} [BEq α] (xs : List α) : List α :=
  (xs.filter fun x => xs.count x > 1).eraseDups

/-- The defects of one scene's declared facts. -/
def sceneDefects (s : Scene) : List String :=
  let at_ := s!"scene t={s.t}"
  (s.intents.flatMap fun d =>
    let who := s!"{at_}: intent record ({d.vehicle}, {d.target})"
    (if s.tracks.contains d.vehicle then [] else [s!"{who}: vehicle {d.vehicle} is not a road user of the scene"]) ++
    (if (s.structure? d.target).isSome then [] else [s!"{who}: target {d.target} is not a structure of the scene"]) ++
    ((duplicates (d.values.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` listed more than once") ++
    ((d.values.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!IntId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` is not a well-formed intention id")) ++
  ((duplicates (s.intents.map fun d => (d.vehicle, d.target))).map fun (v, r) => s!"{at_}: more than one intent record for ({v}, {r})") ++
  (s.structures.flatMap fun st =>
    (if st.kind.isAbstract then [s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} is labelled `{st.kind}`, an abstract kind; label it with a kind that refines `{st.kind}`"] else []) ++
    ((st.unobservedKinds.filter (·.isAbstract)).eraseDups.map fun k =>
      s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} lists `{k}` among unobserved_kinds, an abstract kind; list the kinds refining it that the source cannot tell")) ++
  ((duplicates (s.assumptions.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{at_}: assumption `{id}` listed more than once") ++
  ((s.assumptions.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!AsmId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{at_}: `{id}` is not a well-formed assumption id")

/-- Accepted links that give a track two successors or two predecessors. -/
def linkDefects (τ : Array Scene) (gap : Q) : List String :=
  let links := Grounding.acceptedLinks τ gap
  ((duplicates (links.map (·.1))).map fun t =>
    s!"track {t} is continued by more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.1 == t)}") ++
  ((duplicates (links.map (·.2))).map fun t =>
    s!"track {t} continues more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.2 == t)}")

/-- Every defect of the trace as written; empty for a trace every evaluation may read. -/
def defects (τ : Trace) (gap : Q) : List String :=
  τ.flatMap sceneDefects ++ linkDefects τ.toArray gap

end Admission
end TrafficSpec

1	/-
2	  TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders
3	  Scenarios for witnesses and tests: a scene and a trace from a few named quantities, padding by
4	  timestamp, masking under a manifest, and the `Scenario` a witness file declares.
5	
6	  A witness must be indistinguishable from adapter output to an atom, so everything here goes
7	  through the `World` constructors and nothing else. Reachable from `Witness/**` and `Tests/**`
8	  only: a rule that could build its own evidence proves nothing.
9	
10	  No default magnitude lives here — every extent, speed and distance is an argument the witness
11	  writes through a `Units` constructor.
12	-/
13	import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Monitor
14	
15	namespace TrafficSpec
16	namespace Build
17	
18	/-- Cardinal unit headings in the world frame (+x east, +y north). -/
19	def east : Vec := (Q.ofInt 1, Q.zero)
20	def west : Vec := (Q.ofInt (-1), Q.zero)
21	def north : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt 1)
22	def south : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt (-1))
23	
24	def scale (h : Vec) (k : Q) : Vec := (Q.mul h.1 k, Q.mul h.2 k)
25	
26	/-- A road user with position, heading and speed; velocity follows the heading, path length
27	    is the caller's (cumulative) figure, extents are half-length/half-width/half-height. -/
28	def user (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) (heading : Vec) (speed : Q)
29	    (halfExtent : Q × Q × Q) (pathLength : Option Q := none) : RoadUser :=
30	  { track := track
31	    classes := some classes
32	    kin := { position := some pos
33	             heading := some heading
34	             velocity := some (scale heading speed)
35	             speed := some speed
36	             extent := some halfExtent
37	             pathLength := pathLength } }
38	
39	/-- A road user of which only the position (and classes) was observed. -/
40	def sparseUser (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) : RoadUser :=
41	  { track := track, classes := some classes, kin := { position := some pos } }
42	
43	def withSignals (u : RoadUser) (f : Signals → Signals) : RoadUser := { u with sig := f u.sig }
44	def withKin (u : RoadUser) (f : Kin → Kin) : RoadUser := { u with kin := f u.kin }
45	/-- A measured relation from `a` to `b`, with the measured fields the source supplies. -/
46	def relation (a b : TrackId) (f : MeasuredRelation → MeasuredRelation := id) : MeasuredRelation := f { a := a, b := b }
47	def withRelations (s : Scene) (rs : List MeasuredRelation) : Scene := { s with relations := rs }
48	
49	/-- A region of a kind with a polygon boundary. -/
50	def region (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (boundary : List Vec) : Structure :=
51	  { id := id, kind := kind, boundary := some boundary }
52	/-- An axis-aligned rectangular region from two corners. -/
53	def rect (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (x0 y0 x1 y1 : Q) : Structure :=
54	  region id kind [(x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1)]
55	/-- A lane with its direction and neighbours. -/
56	def lane (id : RegionId) (boundary : List Vec) (direction : Vec)
57	    (left right : Option RegionId := none) (ordinal count : Option Nat := none)
58	    (leadsTo : Option (List RegionId) := none) (enters : Option RegionId := none) : Structure :=
59	  { id := id
60	    kind := .lane
61	    boundary := some boundary
62	    lane := some { direction := some direction, leftNeighbour := left, rightNeighbour := right,
63	                   ordinalFromLeft := ordinal, countInDirection := count, leadsTo := leadsTo,
64	                   entersIntersection := enters } }
65	def point (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (pos : Vec) : Structure :=
66	  { id := id, kind := kind, position := some pos }
67	
68	def device (id : DeviceId) (kind : DeviceKind) (governs : List RegionId) (pos : Option Vec := none) : Device :=
69	  { id := id, kind := kind, governs := governs, position := pos }
70	def signal (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (shows : List SignalIndication) : Device :=
71	  { device id .trafficSignal governs with indications := some shows }
72	def sign (id : DeviceId) (kind : DeviceKind) (governs : List RegionId) : Device := device id kind governs
73	def speedLimit (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (value : Q) (kind : SpeedSignKind) : Device :=
74	  { device id .speedLimitSign governs with speedValue := some value, speedKind := some kind }
75	def zoneSign (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (kind : ZoneKind) (isEnd : Bool)
76	    (conditions : Option Conditions := none) : Device :=
77	  { device id .zoneSign governs with zoneKind := some kind, isEnd := some isEnd, conditions := conditions }
78	
79	/-- Occupancy from the geometry: every user inside every region whose boundary contains its position. -/
80	def occupancyFromGeometry (users : List RoadUser) (structures : List Structure) : List (TrackId × RegionId) :=
81	  users.flatMap fun u =>
82	    match u.kin.position with
83	    | none => []
84	    | some p => structures.filterMap fun st =>
85	      match st.boundary with
86	      | some poly => if Geom.inPolygon p poly then some (u.track, st.id) else none
87	      | none => none
88	
89	/-- A scene; occupancy is derived from geometry unless given. -/
90	def scene (t : Timestamp) (subject : Option TrackId) (users : List RoadUser) (structures : List Structure)
91	    (devices : List Device) (occupies : Option (List (TrackId × RegionId)) := none)
92	    (env : Env := {}) (assumptions : List (AsmId × Bool) := []) (intents : List DeclaredIntent := []) : Scene :=
93	  { t := t
94	    subject := subject
95	    users := users
96	    structures := structures
97	    devices := devices
98	    occupancyObserved := users.map (·.track)
99	    occupies := occupies.getD (occupancyFromGeometry users structures)
100	    env := env
101	    assumptions := assumptions
102	    intents := intents }
103	
104	/-- A trace from a scene generator over instants `t0, t0 + dt, …` (`dt` in seconds). -/
105	def trace (n : Nat) (t0 : Timestamp) (dt : Q) (f : Nat → Timestamp → Scene) : Trace :=
106	  (List.range n).map fun k =>
107	    let t : Timestamp := t0 + (Q.mul (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat k)) (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000))).num /
108	      (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
109	    f k t
110	
111	/-- Repeat the first and last scenes for `before`/`after` seconds at spacing `dt`, so that windows
112	    at the ends of the interesting part are covered rather than truncated. -/
113	def pad (τ : Trace) (before after dt : Q) : Trace :=
114	  match τ.head?, τ.getLast? with
115	  | some first, some last =>
116	    let step : Timestamp := (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).num / (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
117	    let nb := ((Q.div before dt).num / (Q.div before dt).den).toNat
118	    let na := ((Q.div after dt).num / (Q.div after dt).den).toNat
119	    let pre := (List.range nb).reverse.map fun k => { first with t := first.t - step * (k + 1) }
120	    let post := (List.range na).map fun k => { last with t := last.t + step * (k + 1) }
121	    pre ++ τ ++ post
122	  | _, _ => τ
123	
124	def masked (m : Manifest) (τ : Trace) : Trace := maskTrace m τ
125	
126	/-- A manifest that observes every atom except the listed ids (for a `blind` witness). -/
127	def manifest (absent : List String := []) (gap : Q := Q.zero) : Manifest :=
128	  let full := Manifest.full "witness" gap
129	  { full with entries := full.entries.map fun (id, c) => if absent.contains id then (id, .absent) else (id, c) }
130	
131	end Build
132	
133	/-- A witness: a rule, a trace, the reading and manifest it assumes, the grounding it speaks
134	    about (binder ↦ track) and the episode verdict the plan declared over `window` (a closed range
135	    of timestamps; the whole trace when absent). A lookback window is truncated at the start of
136	    every finite trace, so a witness about a rule with one names the instants it speaks about.
137	    A witness is a test of the rule, not evidence about the law: it shows the formulas reach the
138	    verdict it names, on a scene its author built. A history-boundary witness (`boundary` names the
139	    history its trace lacks) shows that the rule stays unknown where the trace does not reach back
140	    far enough to decide it. -/
141	structure Scenario where
142	  name : String
143	  rule : String
144	  trace : Trace
145	  reading : Reading
146	  manifest : Manifest
147	  grounding : List (String × TrackId)
148	  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []   -- an instance's region formals, each a region of the trace
149	  expected : Verdict
150	  window : Option (Timestamp × Timestamp) := none
151	  boundary : String := ""
152	  deriving Repr, Inhabited
153	
154	namespace Scenario
155	/-- The operators that look back from the observation they judge, by the tag their truncation at the
156	    start of a trace carries: only these leave a history-boundary witness unknown. -/
157	def pastOps : List String :=
158	  ["since", "since_rise", "rises", "once", "holdsFor", "atLast", "count", "distance_while", "prim_heading_change",
159	   "heading_since"]
160	
161	/-- The witness holds when the rule's episode verdict on its grounding has the expected tag, and
162	    the verdict is reached for the reason the witness is about: a `notApplicable` witness needs an
163	    instant at which every bound track is present (a track that never appears leaves any rule not
164	    engaged); an `unknown` witness must be unknown only for atoms its manifest masks (an unbound
165	    variable, a truncated window or a missing parameter is a defect, not a masked observation),
166	    except that a history-boundary witness is unknown for a window truncated at the start of its
167	    trace, at least once, and otherwise only for masked atoms; a boundary is declared on an
168	    `unknown` witness only.
169	    The rules are evaluated with their concept calls expanded over `concepts`. A trace the
170	    admission rejects, or a region formal given a region no scene of the trace holds, fails. -/
171	def run (rules : List Rule) (sc : Scenario) (concepts : List Concept := []) : Except String Verdict := do
172	  let rules := rules.map (Concept.expandRule concepts)
173	  let r ← match rules.find? (·.id == sc.rule) with
174	    | some r => pure r
175	    | none => throw s!"{sc.name}: rule {sc.rule} is not registered"
176	  let S ← match Grounding.Setup.admit rules (maskTrace sc.manifest sc.trace) sc.reading sc.manifest.reidGap with
177	    | .ok S => pure S
178	    | .error ds => throw s!"{sc.name}: the trace is not admitted: {"; ".intercalate ds}"
179	  for (n, reg) in sc.regions do
180	    if !(sc.trace.any fun s => (s.structure? reg).isSome) then
181	      throw s!"{sc.name}: region formal `{n}` is region {reg}, which is no structure of the trace"
182	  let g : Grounding.Grounding := ⟨sc.grounding.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Grounding.canon S.cm t)), sc.regions⟩
183	  let tl := Grounding.evaluate S r g
184	  let rows := tl.verdicts.toList.filter fun (t, _) =>
185	    match sc.window with
186	    | some (a, b) => a ≤ t && t ≤ b
187	    | none => true
188	  let got := Grounding.episode (rows.map (·.2))
189	  if !sc.boundary.isEmpty && sc.expected.tag != "unknown" then
190	    throw s!"{sc.name}: a history boundary is declared on a witness that expects {sc.expected.tag}, not unknown"
191	  if got.tag != sc.expected.tag then
192	    throw s!"{sc.name}: expected {sc.expected.tag}, got {got.tag} {(got.reasons.map UnknownReason.tag)}"
193	  match sc.expected with
194	  | .notApplicable =>
195	    if tl.present then pure got
196	    else throw s!"{sc.name}: not applicable, but no instant has every bound track present"
197	  | .unknown _ =>
198	    let absent := sc.manifest.absentIds
199	    let truncated := fun (w : UnknownReason) => match w with | .windowTruncated op => pastOps.contains op | _ => false
200	    let stray := got.reasons.filter fun w => match w with
201	      | .absentAtom n => !(atomIdOf n).any absent.contains
202	      | w => sc.boundary.isEmpty || !truncated w
203	    if !stray.isEmpty then
204	      throw s!"{sc.name}: unknown for {(stray.map UnknownReason.tag)}, not for an atom the manifest masks{if sc.boundary.isEmpty then "" else " or a window truncated at the trace start"}"
205	    else if !sc.boundary.isEmpty && !got.reasons.any truncated then
206	      throw s!"{sc.name}: a history-boundary witness, but no window is truncated at the trace start"
207	    else pure got
208	  | _ => pure got
